Visual Renaissance 01B

Official visual references translated into targeted changes to the existing Asterfall demonstration district.

The shared art direction

The references mix stylized combat imagery, cinematic concepts and highly detailed close-ups. Their common language is credible surface response, strong designed silhouettes and selective magical color. 01B targets that shared language through quieter dark masses, pale mineral structure, pointed architectural profiles, cyan/violet crystal energy and a silver/cyan drake. Saturation and emission are concentrated around focal details.

Pale mineral stoneBlue-charcoal recessesAged bronzeAmethyst accentsCyan energySilver creature scales

Swatches describe roles, not measured final rendered colors. Tone mapping, lighting, weather and material settings affect the actual game.

Actual module changes

These pairs show the actual Master 01 and 01B OBJ geometry with the same neutral offline view and scale within each pair. Pointed arches, mineral crowns and simpler broad structural planes move the existing kit toward R04/R05. The refinement uses fewer unique source triangles, not a larger object-count target.

Not Unity rendering, lighting, materials, scene composition or gameplay evidence. 23 model resources remain; eight were revised. Unique-kit totals are not the number of triangles placed in the live scene.

Actual surface-map changes

Representative raw albedo maps from the two project versions. Normal and packed surface maps were also revised. These are texture-file comparisons without scene lighting; they do not prove final material quality in Unity.

Sandstone

Paler mineral stone with separated joints and more directional variation.

Basalt

Blue-charcoal stone and varied polish, also used by the bounded promenade road surface.

Bronze

Aged metal variation and restrained patina for readable material separation.

Ceramic

Teal mineral glaze with a runtime violet variant for selected architectural accents.

Bark

Darker crevices and more defined organic directional variation for existing trees.

Fabric

Quieter plum textile surfacing for existing canopies.

All library maps remain 512 x 512. The private drake surface generates its own runtime palette and scale maps; the library dragonHide/dragonWing maps are not the active drake material.

Remaining production art

These are proposed acquisition or authoring packages. They are not newly delivered production assets. Detailed handoff and acceptance requirements are in REMAINING_PRODUCTION_ASSETS.md, beside this report.

P0

Hero architecture and surface kit

One sculpted/artist-authored frontage with true recesses, trim atlas, planned wear, clean UVs, LODs and collision proxies; approve a playable camera-distance sample before multiplying it.

P0

Production dragon and animations

Original sculpt, retopology, baked regional detail, eye/membrane materials, clean skinning and authored facial/wing/landing polish compatible with existing gameplay timing.

P0

Hero and NPC pilot set

Detailed bodies, faces, hair, armor, cloth/leather/metal surfacing and first-person hand/weapon presentation integrated with the current controls and animation systems.

P1

Manor room and mystical grove pilots

One navigable amethyst hall with room-state variants; a small tree/root/foliage/rock/stream kit with believable crystal attachment and deliberate routes.

P1

Crystals and complete spell family

Original growth silhouettes and authored cast/trail/impact/sustain/summon phases with sound, readable telegraphs, near-camera handling and graphics tiers.

P2

Realm landmarks and expanded creature art

Approved original hero silhouettes, distant architecture/terrain and sky content, followed by scoped rigged creatures. These remain future production work.

Approve one representative frontage, grove corner, drake close-up and short effect sequence in the actual game before expanding the style across the world.

Unity tests and visual review still required

  1. Fresh import and compilation. Open Unity 6000.3.16f1, resolve packages, verify no Console or shader errors, correct importer settings and no magenta materials. Run the full EditMode suite including district/creature tests. Offline syntax parsing is not semantic compilation.
  2. Matched visual captures. Capture Master 01 and 01B at the same seed, time, weather, FOV, position, resolution and quality: street wide, first-person arch close-up, dusk/night crystal frontage, rooftop garden and drake close-up. None has yet been captured in Unity.
  3. Cameras and interface. Walk, aim, sprint, drive and fly in first person and third person, with the HUD visible at 1080p, 1440p and ultrawide. Inspect near-plane clipping, target visibility, canopy/balcony clearance, reticle contrast and particle trail obstruction.
  4. Gameplay preservation. Regression-test story/quests, save/load, cover, bullet traces, traffic, creature weak points, hit flash, folded wings, attack poses and rooftop exhibit behavior. The refined decoration remains visual; original colliders are retained.
  5. Weather and lifecycle. Compare noon, dusk, night, rain and sandstorm, then leave the district and cross realm/region boundaries. Re-enter Play Mode with domain reload on and off; check reset cleanup and resource leaks.
  6. Measured desktop cost. Compare the same 60-second path on the same desktop: CPU/GPU frame time and p95, draw calls, triangles, allocations, memory, boot time and LOD transitions. No fps or hardware-minimum claim is made.
  7. Player and renderer matrix. Build and test the Windows player, shader retention and all required editor/player, input-mode and renderer configurations. After Built-in acceptance, repeat visual and performance checks using the optional URP workflow.
